metadata.title: Rafeeq — Your offline AI companion
metadata.description: Rafeeq is a fully offline, local AI desktop assistant for code help, document Q&A, and summarization — built for air-gapped and network-restricted machines.

footer.description: A fully offline AI companion for code help, document Q&A and summarization.

home.title: Your fully offline AI companion
home.subtitle: Rafeeq is a local AI desktop assistant for code help, document Q&A, and summarization — built for machines that will never see the open internet.
home.highlight1Description: Rafeeq makes no network calls at runtime, by design and by construction. Block your network and it runs identically.
home.highlight2Description: Powered by llama.cpp and quantized GGUF models on CPU — no GPU required, no API keys, no cloud.
home.highlight3Description: Corporate VMs, air-gapped networks, regulated industries — Rafeeq works where cloud AI tools can't.
home.bannerTitle: No API keys. No cloud calls. No telemetry.
home.bannerSubtitle: The model, the runtime, and your data never leave the machine — verifiably, not just by policy.
home.caption: {size} installer · MIT licensed · macOS and Linux on the way
home.ctaTitle: Get Rafeeq on a machine that has no internet.
home.ctaBody: Install it, copy a model file over by USB or file share, and start chatting.
home.blockDocsBody: Load a local .txt, .md, .docx or .pdf file and ask about its contents, or get a summary. For whole folders, index them with local RAG. Everything is computed on-device.
home.blockOfflineTitle: Don't take our word for it.
home.offlineStep1: Block network access: a firewall rule, a disabled adapter or an air-gapped VM.
home.offlineStep2: Launch Rafeeq and load a model.
home.shotAlt: The Rafeeq chat screen with a local model loaded, running offline.

features.title: Everything Rafeeq can do
features.subtitle: All of it runs on-device. Nothing here needs — or uses — an internet connection.
features.chatDescription: Prompt in, streamed response out, powered by a small quantized model running on CPU. No account, no rate limits, no usage sent anywhere. Set the default temperature, response length and CPU threads in Settings.
features.managerDescription: Point Rafeeq at a sideloaded .gguf file, swap models, and see size and quantization info at a glance. Save named profiles for quick switching. Chat and embedding models are labelled automatically.
features.codeDescription: Paste or select code, ask questions, get explanations or suggestions. Chat and explain only — Rafeeq never executes code.
features.docDescription: Load a local .txt, .md, .docx, or .pdf file and ask questions about its contents or get a summary. Long documents are truncated to fit the model's context.
features.ragDescription: Index a folder of documents with a sideloaded embedding model, then ask questions answered from the most relevant retrieved passages — all computed on-device. Folders are managed on the Knowledge base page, and each answer lists the passages it used.
features.sessionDescription: Conversations are saved automatically and can be resumed from the sidebar, so nothing is lost between sessions. Search past chats, or delete them all from Settings.
features.offlineDescription: An in-app indicator and a hand-maintained dependency allowlist confirm no network-capable plugin is registered in the build. Block your network — Rafeeq runs identically.
features.goodIntro: What Rafeeq does and doesn't do today, stated plainly.
features.good1Body: Rafeeq never executes code, in code-help mode or anywhere else.
features.good2Body: Small quantized GGUF models run on ordinary machines through llama.cpp.
features.good3Body: The standard installer includes none. The other installer includes a small starter model, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct.
features.good4Body: Only the beginning of a long document fits the model's context (about 2,000 words). Rafeeq tells you when this happens.
features.good5Body: macOS and Linux builds are on the way.
features.ctaTitle: See it run with the network off.
features.ctaBody: Install Rafeeq, block network access, and chat.

download.title: Download Rafeeq
download.subtitle: Two installers are published. Both behave identically once a model is loaded — you can always add or switch models later.
download.standardDescription: The standard installer. No model included — you sideload a .gguf file yourself after installing.
download.standardBestFor: Air-gapped machines, restricted networks, or if you already know which model you want to use.
download.bundledDescription: Includes a small starter model (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct) that installs automatically on first launch. Nothing to configure.
download.bundledBestFor: Anyone on a normal internet-connected machine who wants to start chatting immediately.
download.footer: macOS and Linux builds are on the way. Source is available on
download.offlineTitle: Installing on a machine with no internet
download.offlineIntro: Use the standard installer and bring the model over yourself.
download.offlineStep1Body: Get the standard installer, and a .gguf model file from Hugging Face. A file ending in Q4_K_M is a good balance of size and quality.
download.offlineStep2Body: Use a USB drive or an internal file share.
download.offlineStep3Body: Open Rafeeq, go to Models, choose Open models folder, drop the file in, then click Refresh.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.step1Description: Download the installer for your platform from the <downloadLink>Download page</downloadLink>. If you're not sure which variant to pick, the one with the starter model included is the easiest way to get going.
docs.step2Description: If you installed the standard build, Rafeeq needs at least one .gguf model file before it can chat:
docs.step2List1: Go to huggingface.co and search for a model with GGUF in the name.
docs.step2List2: Download a quantized file — one named like *.Q4_K_M.gguf is a good balance of size and quality.
docs.step2List3: Open Rafeeq, go to the Models screen, and click Open models folder. Drop the file in, then click Refresh.
docs.step3Description: Load a model from the Models screen, then pick a mode — General, Code help, Document, or RAG — depending on what you're working on.
docs.ragDescription: RAG needs a second, small embedding model (not your chat model), for example nomic-embed-text-v1.5. Sideload it the same way as a chat model, open the Knowledge base page, select it as the embedding model and add a folder of documents. Indexing runs in the background and can be paused. Then ask questions in RAG mode.
docs.offlineDescription: Rafeeq makes zero network calls at runtime, by construction. You can test this yourself: block network access at the OS level (firewall rule, disabled adapter, or an air-gapped VM) and Rafeeq will run identically. The app also shows an offline status indicator in the header.
